Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, September 15-16, 2026

Published 2026-10-06 22:30 UTC

The Federal Open Market Committee on Wednesday released the minutes of its meeting held September 15 and 16, 2026. The minutes describe the discussions of participants about economic conditions, the outlook, and the Committee's balance sheet policy.

Participants observed that economic activity had continued to expand at a moderate pace, with consumer spending supported by real income growth. Many participants noted that business investment in equipment had softened, while spending on data centers and related infrastructure remained strong. Several participants commented that housing activity remained weak because of elevated mortgage rates.

Regarding the labor market, participants noted that payroll growth had slowed and that the unemployment rate had edged up over the summer. Most participants judged that labor market conditions were roughly in balance, though some saw signs that hiring had cooled more than expected in sectors sensitive to interest rates.

Participants observed that inflation had moved down over the past year but remained somewhat elevated. Several noted that services inflation excluding housing had been slow to decline. Some participants expressed concern that tariffs and higher energy prices could keep goods inflation from falling further in the near term.

In their discussion of the balance sheet, participants considered the pace of runoff of securities holdings. Many participants judged it appropriate to slow the pace of runoff of Treasury securities in coming months to ensure a smooth transition to ample reserves. A few participants preferred to continue at the current pace, noting that money market conditions remained calm.

Participants agreed that monetary policy would remain data dependent and that the Committee would carefully assess incoming information, the evolving outlook and the balance of risks. The minutes note that members' views are summarized in the Summary of Economic Projections released after the meeting.
